questions.prompt: What does the Born rule give for an amplitude alpha in the Z basis?
questions.explanation: The probability is the squared magnitude of the amplitude.

options.text: One complete prepare, operate and measure trial

questions.explanation: A shot is one experimental trial whose detector produces one recorded outcome.

questions.prompt: If 70 zeros and 30 ones are mapped to +1 and -1, what is the expectation estimate?
What usually happens to sampling uncertainty as shots increase?
questions.explanation: Independent sampling uncertainty shrinks with the inverse square root of the shot count.

questions.prompt: How can |+> be measured in the X basis using a Z detector?

options.text: Apply H before the Z detector
Measure the same collapsed state repeatedly

questions.explanation: H rotates the X basis into the computational basis, so H followed by Z measurement analyzes X.

questions.prompt: Why does measuring a state and then repeating the same measurement differ from fresh shots?

options.text: The first measurement can collapse the state
The Born rule changes its formula

questions.explanation: After an ideal outcome, the system is in the corresponding basis state for an immediate repeat.

questions.prompt: A 16-shot run expected to have 12 zeros produces 11. What is the best interpretation?

options.text: A normal finite sample can fluctuate
The probability must be exactly 11/16 forever

questions.explanation: Expected counts are not guarantees. One sample can differ from the exact model.

questions.prompt: What can more shots not fix by themselves?

options.text: A systematic device bias or wrong circuit

questions.explanation: More samples reduce random uncertainty but do not repair a biased device or incorrect experiment.
